properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 28 at 8:45AM PST until December 1 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
Another round of rainfall is expected to begin late Sunday night
into Monday, bringing another 2 to 3 inches of rain to the Olympic
Basin. The Skokomish River near Potlatch will rise again in response.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Recent rains and saturated ground will cause flooding to occur
more readily, particularly for the Skokomish River near Potlatch
where minor flooding is possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and
seas 8 to 11 feet.

* WHERE...Pohnpei Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM ChST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Surging trade winds of 15 to 25 knots with
gusts to 30 knots will continue today, and frequent strong gusts

trade-wind swell is expected to bring seas hazardous to small
craft operations to Pohnpei waters today, with sea heights
peaking at around 11 feet this afternoon, then subside slightly.

least early Tuesday morning.
properties.instruction:

vessels, should avoid boating in hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 28 at 10:48AM AST until November 29 at 8:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern and eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and
Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:31AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.5 feet, then continuing to 6.6 feet early
next week where it is expected to linger into at least mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise through Major Flood
Stage, reaching 6.5 feet late this weekend, then 6.6 feet early
next week. The river is then forecast to remain steady through at
least mid next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:20AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Rainfall working through the basin has caused river levels on the
St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood
Stage, above its previous record flood stage. River levels are
forecast to begin a very slow decline within Major flood stage this
weekend and through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 13.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain within Major Flood
Stage. A slow decline from 13.1 feet may begin over the weekend
into early next week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:13AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Past heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 4.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 4.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to remain generally steady
between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Bristol and Plymouth
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 AM EST Saturday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 AM EST Saturday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 600 PM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 4:11PM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2
feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 27 at 4:06PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Some
locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHERE...Much of central California.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading
to a high transportation risk.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog will resemble that of the past two
days. Low clouds will quickly become dense fog shortly after
sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this
evening, if you are traveling.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your low beam headlights, and leave plenty
of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
